review: 2026-08 round-9 — findings raised while porting crust's prose guard (tests/docsLint.test.ts, tests/skillsDocs.test.ts, the website's lint-examples.mjs); then extended by a full dogfood of every plane against mybodycorpai/apps/web
method: Not a review pass. These are the defects the new documentation guard found on its first run, plus what verifying them turned up. Every entry was reproduced by running the tool over tests/fixtures/nextapp and inspecting the emitted files — none is reasoned-only. The guard itself was mutation-probed: six drifts were introduced one at a time (each applied by a script asserting match count == 1, reverted after), the unmutated baseline was run first and printed, and all six were caught; survivors: 0. The second half is a dogfood: the SHIPPED binary regenerated mybodycorpai/apps/web (99 files, 183 components) and every plane was run — unit 517 pass/14 skip, browser 191/12, perf 256/319 skip (every skip carrying a reason), e2e 39 pass, load 33 pass. Green runs were probed for vacuity rather than believed: the e2e landing assertion was inverted to prove the session is authenticated, and the load plane was re-run against a deliberately dead cookie.

severityAnchors.P0: emitted suite broken, silently passes, or lies; or the tool corrupts user files
severityAnchors.P1: wrong analysis output, docs claim contradicted by code, or a CI gap that lets P0s ship
severityAnchors.P2: performance, DX, error-message quality, design friction
severityAnchors.P3: opportunity aligned with the product's spirit

findings.title: Two thirds of the inline sidecar's reports map pointed at files no run has ever written
findings.claim: <Component>.flawless.json carries a 'reports' map so a reader can jump from the summary to the full report. It named reports/<Component>.a11y.json and reports/<Component>.react-rules.json. Neither is ever created: both tasks are SWEEPS that write one aggregate for the whole run — src/tasks/a11yScan.ts:15 aggregateFile 'a11y.json', src/tasks/eslintReactRules.ts:14 'react-rules.json'. Only perfStatic was correct. Reproduced: a --tasks perf-static,a11y,react-rules run over tests/fixtures/nextapp gives a sidecar whose a11y and reactRules paths do not exist (perfStatic does), while reports/ holds a11y.json, react-rules.json, <C>.perf-static.json and summary.json.
findings.spirit: A pointer to a file that was never written is a quiet lie in an artefact whose whole job is to be believed. It also propagated: the published website documented per-component a11y and react-rules reports, and the shapes it listed for them were the perf-static shape, because the docs were written from this field.
findings.foundBy: the new docs guard — check G, 'emitted artefact paths named in prose are really emitted'
findings.note: The sidecar had no test of any kind, which is why the wrong names survived every previous round.
findings.fix: The aggregate basenames are now exported (A11Y_REPORT, REACT_RULES_REPORT) and the sidecar composes from them, so renaming an aggregate cannot leave the pointer behind. Regression test in tests/emittedPaths.test.ts asserts every path in every sidecar's reports map exists after a real run; probed by reverting the fix (match count == 1) and confirming it reddens.

findings.title: The inline sidecar stores ABSOLUTE report paths (narrower than first stated)
findings.claim: The reports map holds machine-rooted paths. CORRECTION to this entry as first written: it claimed the sidecar 'is committed', which is wrong in the mode that matters. The tool itself adds `*.flawless.json` to the project's .gitignore (src/core.ts:557), so in --nextjs mode — the mode the dogfood app and the documented workflow use — sidecars are never committed. Verified on mybodycorpai: 181 sidecars on disk, 0 tracked. The finding survives only OUTSIDE --nextjs mode, where updateGitignore is not reached at all: reproduced by running `--tasks perf-static` over a non-Next fixture in a fresh git repo, after which `git add -A` stages 5 sidecars carrying absolute paths.
findings.spirit: Same class as the three defects emitPaths.ts's header records, in the one emitted file its sentinel sweep does not cover.
findings.foundBy: re-reading the entry while answering 'has this been dogfooded?' — the dogfood app disproved it
findings.note: Recorded as a correction, not an edit: the original entry asserted a scope wider than the code supports, which is the exact defect class this ledger exists to catch. Downgraded P2 -> P3.

findings.title: a11y and react-rules were dead in the SHIPPED binary on any monorepo
findings.claim: resolveBiomeBin checked the tool's own node_modules, then exactly <cwd>/node_modules/.bin/biome, then PATH. A monorepo hoists dev dependencies to the workspace root, so apps/web/node_modules/.bin/biome does not exist while <root>/node_modules/.bin/biome does. Reproduced on mybodycorpai with the published 0.3.0+c5537b6 binary: a11y and react-rules both ok:false, 'biome executable not found', exit 1 — while the SAME command under the source install exited 0 with both tasks green, because a source install resolves biome from flawless-react's own node_modules. Two of seven tasks were broken in the shipped artifact and working in the artifact every previous dogfood had used.
findings.spirit: The compiled binary is the product. A defect that only the shipped form exhibits, and that the testing form cannot see, is the worst shape a defect can have here.
findings.foundBy: round-9 dogfood — first run of the repro line with the published binary rather than from source
findings.note: The file's own header records a previous fix for the compiled-binary case; it added the scanned package but never walked up. The dogfood app is a monorepo, so this was reachable the whole time and was masked by how the dogfood was run.
findings.fix: Candidates now walk from the scanned package to the filesystem root — node's own resolution order. Verified on mybodycorpai: all seven tasks ok:true, exit 0. The first test written for this was VACUOUS (it covered the helper, so reverting the resolver's use of it stayed green); it now covers biomeCandidates, the list the resolver consumes, and the same reversion reddens it.

findings.title: The load plane reports healthy percentiles for a login page when LOAD_AUTH expires
findings.claim: crust follows redirects, so an expired session turns every route into the login page answering 200. The emitted pipe is `… | GET $LOAD_BASE<route> -H "$LOAD_AUTH" | expect 200 | stats`, so expect 200 passes and stats reports real-looking numbers. Reproduced against the dogfood app's production build with a deliberately dead cookie: {"count":20,"status":{"200":20},"p50":19.7,"p95":23.6}, exit 0, every request served /login. Nothing downstream can see it — in load mode crust's record is {status, ms, url} and that url is the REQUESTED one, byte-identical whether the session is live or dead (verified by asserting false and reading the record under both).
findings.spirit: B-12 in the load plane: green before it is real. docs/e2e-and-api.md already described this hazard and told the reader to prove auth by hand; nothing enforced it.
findings.foundBy: round-9 dogfood — the anti-vacuous probe the flawless-e2e-load skill calls for
findings.note: The dogfood app was NOT vulnerable: its owner had already hit this and hand-written flawless/load/routes.setup.ts, which checks an authenticated /api/me and fails loudly. That file is tracked at main and the tool emits nothing like it — the app was protected, the tool was not. The hand-written module is also where the fix's shape comes from.
findings.fix: The load task now emits flawless/load/routes.setup.ts — crust awaits a pipes file's sibling setup module before any line runs. It seeds every LOAD_<PARAM> from params.json (replacing the env.sh sourcing step, whose own comments record two incidents of exporting nothing SILENTLY while the pipes measured the 404 handler) and probes EVERY static route, throwing if one lands elsewhere. Every static route, not one: the first cut picked a single route, drew /forgot-password on the dogfood app — a public page a dead cookie does not redirect — and would have been a check that cannot fail. WRITE-ONCE, so the hand-written module above is kept; written when absent, so existing suites gain it. Verified end to end on the real app: valid cookie 33 pass/0 fail exit 0; dead cookie exit 2 naming the route and where it landed; --force leaves the hand-written one byte-identical.

findings.title: Outside --nextjs mode the tool ignores nothing it generates
findings.claim: updateGitignore is called only inside the Next.js branch, so a plain `flawless-react "src/**/*.tsx"` run adds no ignore entries at all — not reports/, not heaps/, not playwright-report/, not e2e/.auth.json, whose own emitted comment calls it session cookies staged for commit. Reproduced in a fresh git repo over a non-Next fixture: after one run `git add -A` stages 28 generated files. In --nextjs mode all ten entries are added correctly.
findings.spirit: The tool writing files a user then commits by accident is the tool's problem, not theirs.
findings.foundBy: reproducing FR-049, which turned out to be a special case of this
findings.note: Not fixed here: the ignore list is composed from outDirRel against nextCtx.root, and the non-Next path has no equivalent notion of a project root to resolve against. Choosing one is a design decision, not a patch.

docsDriftFixed: README.md — the CLI reference table omitted --app-resolver, -h/--help and -V/--version: three of 26 flags absent from a table presented as the reference.
website src/pages/docs/cli.mdx — the table headed 'Every flag flawless-react accepts' omitted --roots, --exclude, --no-default-excludes and --ci for a whole release.

website cli.mdx, index.mdx, quickstart.mdx, generated-suite.mdx — all four documented per-component a11y and react-rules reports (FR-048's downstream), and generated-suite.mdx additionally gave both of them the perf-static field shape instead of their real one.

docs/e2e-and-api.md and the flawless-e2e-load skill still told readers to `source flawless/load/env.sh` and named jq a hard prerequisite; both are obsolete now that routes.setup.ts seeds the ids, and the manual 'prove it authenticates' step is enforced.
gapsNotTaken: `bun run <script>` names in prose are not checked. Three kinds appear — this repo's, the generated suite's, and the dogfood app's — and only an allowlist could tell them apart, which would rot faster than the claims it guarded. Stated in the test header rather than left implicit.

The website lint checks examples and the flag table. It does not check emitted artefact paths, which would need it to run a generation; the repo-side check G covers that surface for the repo's own prose only.
This repo has no AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md, though the round-9 review prompt tells a reviewer to start with one. docs/architecture.md is the nearest thing and now carries the guard's entry point.
